xBRIEFInfo.author: overdeck/0.0.0
xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-1897: bug(cli): pan start workspace-prep hangs/times out (>120s) on re-entry — blocks PAN-1711, PAN-1827 (no spawn, no error)

plan.title: bug(cli): pan start workspace-prep hangs/times out (>120s) on re-entry — blocks PAN-1711, PAN-1827 (no spawn, no error)
plan.author: agent:claude-fable-5

narratives.Problem: pan start on an existing workspace can exceed outer supervisor kill budgets (120-200s) during 'Preparing workspace...' with zero visible progress and no error. Root cause (verified): (1) ora 8 disables spinner.text rendering when stdout is not a TTY, so non-interactive callers see only the initial line — slow progress is indistinguishable from a hang; (2) several prep steps are unbounded — git fetch/merge and the husky-hooked auto-commit inside syncMainIntoWorkspace (src/lib/cloister/merge-agent.ts:1259) carry no execAsync timeout, tracker API calls have no explicit timeout, and spawnAgent can run a full inline docker rebuildWorkspaceStack; (3) RUN-35 host load made those steps genuinely slow (a 300s budget succeeded — contention, not deadlock).
narratives.Proposal: Add a CLI prep-progress module (src/cli/commands/start-prep-progress.ts) that wraps each prep phase with a step budget, emits plain [prep] stdout lines for non-TTY callers plus a 15s still-running heartbeat, and rejects with an error naming the step and budget on exhaustion. Wire the four phases in start.ts (state-reconcile 60s fail-fast, sync-main 240s degrade, tracker-context 60s degrade, spawn 600s fail-fast). Independently, add explicit execAsync timeouts to every git operation inside syncMainIntoWorkspace/autoCommitWorkspaceChangesBeforeSync with timeout-aware failure reasons and a best-effort merge --abort on merge timeout. Document the budgets and heartbeat in the pan-start skill.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No parallelization or caching of prep steps (bun install caching, concurrent fetch) — follow-up optimization
- No new CLI flags or config keys for budgets (constants only)
- No changes to the remote/fly.io workspace path
- No changes to the planning-session (start-planning) streaming path
- No global whole-command watchdog — bounds are per-step
- No changes to the flywheel's own outer command budgets (docs guidance only)

autoDecisions.summary: Chose heartbeat + per-step bounded prep over prep parallelization
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue's refinement comment establishes contention (not deadlock) and names the heartbeat-instrumented-timeout direction as the likely fix; parallelization is an optimization deferred to NonGoals.

autoDecisions.summary: Budgets are module constants (state-reconcile 60s, sync-main 240s outer / fetch 60s / merge 120s / commit 60s / status 30s, tracker 60s, spawn 600s, heartbeat 15s) with no new flags
autoDecisions.rationale: No configurability was requested; constants keep the CLI/skill surface unchanged and satisfy fail-fast-with-clear-reason acceptance. Spawn gets 600s because inline docker rebuilds are legitimately slow.

autoDecisions.summary: sync-main and tracker-context timeouts degrade (warn + continue); state-reconcile and spawn timeouts fail fast
autoDecisions.rationale: start.ts already continues on sync-main failure so the agent resolves conflicts (PAN-1872); tracker context already has non-fatal fallbacks. The migration gate and the spawn itself have no degraded mode.

autoDecisions.summary: A timed-out git merge is classified as a timeout, not conflicts, and triggers best-effort git merge --abort
autoDecisions.rationale: The existing catch treats any merge throw as conflicts; letting a SIGTERM-killed merge enter the conflict path would mislabel the failure and skip cleanup.

items.title: Add start-prep-progress module: step budgets, non-TTY [prep] lines, 15s heartbeat

narrative.Action: Create src/cli/commands/start-prep-progress.ts exporting createPrepProgress(spinner, opts?) -> { update(text), step(name, budgetMs, fn) } and PrepStepTimeoutError. update() always sets spinner.text and, when the output stream is not a TTY, also writes a plain '[prep] <text>' line to stdout. step() emits a start line, runs a 15s setInterval heartbeat ('[prep] still running: <name> (Ns elapsed)', non-TTY only), races fn() against setTimeout(budgetMs), clears timers on settle, emits a completion line with elapsed seconds, and rejects with PrepStepTimeoutError whose message names the step and budget (e.g. "Prep step 'sync-main' exceeded its 240s budget"). The raced fn() keeps running after timeout — callers decide fail-fast vs degrade. Unit tests use vi.useFakeTimers() + advanceTimersByTimeAsync exclusively (repo fake-timers rule; never real waits).

items.title: Given a non-TTY stream, when update('Syncing latest main into workspace...') is called, the module writes a '[prep] Syncing latest main into workspace...' line to the stream and sets spinner.text to the same text
Given a TTY stream, when update() is called, the module sets spinner.text and emits no '[prep]' plain line
Given a step whose fn is still pending after 15s (fake timers), the module emits a still-running heartbeat line naming the step and elapsed seconds, and repeats it every 15s until the step settles
Given a step whose fn exceeds budgetMs (fake timers), step() rejects with PrepStepTimeoutError whose message names the step and the budget in seconds

Given a step whose fn resolves within budget, step() returns fn's value, clears the heartbeat interval and timeout (no timer leaks under fake timers), and emits a completion line with elapsed duration
Wire the four pan start prep phases through prep.step() with budgets and fail-fast/degrade semantics

narrative.Action: In src/cli/commands/start.ts, create const prep = createPrepProgress(spinner) right after the ora spinner at line 838, route the prep-flow spinner.text mutations through prep.update(), and wrap exactly four phases in prep.step(): (1) 'state-reconcile', 60_000ms, around requireAutomaticStateMigration + applyStartPolicyOptions (start.ts:845-848) — a PrepStepTimeoutError propagates to the outer catch (start.ts:1296-1298) which spinner.fail()s and exits 1; (2) 'sync-main', 240_000ms, around syncMainIntoWorkspace (start.ts:1042) — catch PrepStepTimeoutError alongside the existing syncErr catch (start.ts:1056-1058): spinner.warn naming the phase and budget, then continue to spawn (existing degraded semantics, PAN-1872); (3) 'tracker-context', 60_000ms, around getTrackerContext (start.ts:1210) — on timeout, spinner.warn and proceed with '' as trackerContext; (4) 'spawn', 600_000ms, around spawnAgent (start.ts:1222) — timeout propagates to the outer catch, failing fast with the step-naming message. Expose budget constants from start-prep-progress.ts or a small constants block; export any new pure helper through __testInternals for the wiring test. New test tests/unit/cli/start-prep-wiring.test.ts asserts the degrade-vs-fail-fast mapping using mocked step functions and fake timers.

items.title: When pan start runs with non-TTY stdout, each of the four bounded phases (state-reconcile, sync-main, tracker-context, spawn) emits a '[prep]' step-start line before the phase executes
When the sync-main phase exceeds its 240s budget (fake timers), pan start emits a warning naming 'sync-main' and its budget and continues to the spawn phase instead of exiting
When the tracker-context phase exceeds its 60s budget (fake timers), pan start warns naming the phase and builds the work-agent prompt with an empty tracker section, still reaching spawn
When the state-reconcile or spawn phase exceeds its budget (fake timers), pan start exits non-zero and the failure message names the phase and its budget in seconds
Add execAsync timeouts + timeout-aware failure reasons to sync-main git operations

expected_outputs: existing sync-main and auto-commit suites still pass

narrative.Action: In src/lib/cloister/merge-agent.ts add constants SYNC_GIT_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS=60_000, SYNC_GIT_MERGE_TIMEOUT_MS=120_000, SYNC_GIT_COMMIT_TIMEOUT_MS=60_000, SYNC_GIT_STATUS_TIMEOUT_MS=30_000 and pass timeout: options to the execAsync calls at: git fetch origin main (line 1325), git merge origin/main (line 1334), the auto-commit git commit (line 160), and the status/add/reset/diff calls in autoCommitWorkspaceChangesBeforeSync (lines 92-152) and syncMainIntoWorkspace (line 1282+). Add helper describeGitTimeout(error, label, budgetMs): string | null that returns e.g. 'git fetch origin main timed out after 60s' when error.killed === true (node exec timeout kill), else null; export it via a test-internals object. Use it so: fetch timeout returns { success:false, reason: <fetch timeout reason> }; merge timeout is detected BEFORE the conflict classification (the current catch sets hasConflicts=true for any throw), runs best-effort git merge --abort (with the status timeout), and returns { success:false, reason: <merge timeout reason> }; commit timeout makes autoCommitWorkspaceChangesBeforeSync return success:false with a reason naming the commit step (husky hooks stall). Keep the SyncMainResult shape unchanged (shared with src/dashboard/server/routes/workspaces/merge-ops.ts:273); async-only, no execSync. Tests mock the exec layer (vi.mock of child_process/execAsync) rather than spawning slow children; any timer use is fake timers.

items.title: Given the mocked git fetch rejects with killed:true, syncMainIntoWorkspace returns success:false with a reason naming 'git fetch origin main' and the 60s budget instead of waiting indefinitely

Given the mocked git merge rejects with killed:true, syncMainIntoWorkspace runs git merge --abort, does NOT take the conflict path, and returns success:false with a reason naming the merge step and its 120s budget

Given the mocked git commit rejects with killed:true, autoCommitWorkspaceChangesBeforeSync returns success:false with a reason naming the auto-commit step (hook stall) and sync aborts with that reason

Every execAsync git invocation inside syncMainIntoWorkspace and autoCommitWorkspaceChangesBeforeSync passes an explicit timeout option, and the SyncMainResult type is unchanged (existing sync-main and auto-commit suites pass unmodified)
Document prep heartbeat, budgets, and fail-fast/degrade split in the pan-start skill

expected_outputs: lint-skills passes with no flag/subcommand drift reported for pan-start
metadata.acJustification: Docs-only item: the two criteria fully pin the required content (phases/budgets table and heartbeat/semantics example); further ACs would restate them.

narrative.Action: Add a 'Slow or hanging workspace prep' subsection to sync-sources/skills/pan-start/SKILL.md that: (a) lists the four bounded prep phases with their default budgets (state-reconcile 60s, sync-main 240s, tracker-context 60s, spawn 600s); (b) shows a sample '[prep] still running: sync-main (45s elapsed)' heartbeat line and explains these lines appear for non-interactive callers because ora spinner updates render only on a TTY; (c) states that sync-main and tracker-context timeouts degrade (warn + continue to spawn) while state-reconcile and spawn timeouts fail fast with the step named; (d) advises supervisors invoking pan start non-interactively to budget at least 300s under load (RUN-35 finding). Introduce no new flags so scripts/lint-skills.sh needs no changes.

items.title: The pan-start SKILL.md troubleshooting section shows the four bounded prep phases with their default budgets and a sample '[prep]' heartbeat line, and states heartbeat lines appear for non-interactive callers

The section shows which phase timeouts fail fast (state-reconcile, spawn) versus degrade-and-continue (sync-main, tracker-context) and contains the >=300s outer-budget guidance for non-interactive pan start under load
